LD matrices

Source: R/ld-matrix.R
og_ld_matrix.Rd

og_ld_matrix() returns the signed LD correlation r between every pair of variants, read from an LD Store. See vignette("ld").

Usage

og_ld_matrix(src, variants, fill_below_t_far = FALSE)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api() or og_local(), which carries the LD resource.

variants

ALIDs and rsIDs, or a data frame of Associations.

fill_below_t_far

Set pairs below the Far Threshold to 0, as above.

Value

A numeric matrix (class og_ld_matrix, which is also a matrix) with og_provenance() attached: ld (the LD Store that answered), ld_choice ("user", "ancestry_default" or "matched") and absent.

Details

The matrix is named by ALID, on both dimensions; the sign of r refers to the first allele in each name. variants are ALIDs or rsIDs (an rsID stands for every ALID it names), or a data frame of Associations, whose alid column names the variants and whose Analyses' Assigned Ancestry chooses the LD Store when the Source has no LD resource. A variant the LD Store doesn't hold is left out of the matrix, with a warning of class opengwasr_ld_absent_variants (count, ids); they are in og_provenance(m)$absent.

An LD Store doesn't hold every pair: a pair it doesn't hold is NA. One Job takes at most 500 variants; more are split into several Jobs and put back together, so the matrix covers every pair.

With fill_below_t_far = TRUE, a pair of variants on one chromosome, within the LD Store's far_bp of each other, that it doesn't hold (so its r² is below the LD Store's Far Threshold) is set to 0. Pairs further apart, or on different chromosomes, stay NA.

The LD is the Source's LD resource: on the API Source its ld_store (og_api(ld_store = )), else the LD Store matching the Assigned Ancestry of the Associations' Analyses (refused for Unassigned or mixed ancestries, and for variants given without Analyses). For other LD, pass another Source, such as og_api(inherit = src, ld_store = "EUR").

On a Local Source, PLINK computes the matrix on your machine from its PLINK Reference (og_local(bfile = )). Its LD isn't adjusted for principal components, so the first call in a session to read each PLINK Reference warns, with class opengwasr_plink_unadjusted (see og_local()). Variants are matched to the reference by rsID (an ALID by its rsid column, if variants is a data frame that has one, else by the Source's Store Releases' variant table); those with no rsID, or not in the reference, are left out, with a message (class opengwasr_plink_unmatched, count). An LD-only Local Source (og_local(bfile = ) with no gwas) has nothing to look an ALID up in, so ALIDs without an rsid column are refused (class opengwasr_gwas_store_required, with the ALIDs in alids, and the ways round in forms: see og_local()). A Local Source with no LD resource is refused (opengwasr_ld_resource_required). The matrix holds every pair, in the order of variants, and is named <rsid>_<allele>_<allele> with the reference's alleles: the sign of r refers to the first one. fill_below_t_far doesn't apply. Provenance's ld is the reference's path.

A request the LD Store can't answer is refused by the API (opengwasr_ld_refusal, with reason, t_far, near_bp and far_bp); a choice of LD Store that can't be made without guessing is refused by opengwasr (opengwasr_ld_unmatched, with the LD Stores in ld_stores).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api(ld_store = "EUR")
m <- og_ld_matrix(src, c("16:53772541:A:G", "16:53767042:C:T"))
og_provenance(m)$ld
} # }
